name: Biology (Min)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
The Biology minor requires a minimum of six courses meeting the following criteria:

• All courses must be taken for a letter grade (no other grading basis is allowed).

• A minimum total GPA of 2.0 is required in courses taken for the minor.

• All courses must be worth or approved for three or more units.

• At least three courses must be taken at the 100-level or higher. The only courses below 100 that are allowable are one additional BIO 80- level course and OSPAUSTL 10, 28, or 32; note that OSPAUSTL 10, 28, and 32 together count as three courses toward the minor

• The two required 80-series courses for the minor cannot be substituted through transfer credit or any other course (BIO 100-level or higher, approved out-of-department course, or through a submitted General Petition)

• Courses used to fulfill the minor may not be used to satisfy any other department degree requirements (minor or major).

• Stanford Introductory Seminars (IntroSems or Sophomore Seminars) may not be used to fulfill the minor requirements.
Courses that do NOT count toward the minor:

• Foundational lab courses (BIO 43, BIO 44, BIO 45, BIO 46, BIO 47)

• Capstone courses: BIO 196A, 196B, 196C; BIO 199A, 199B, 199C; BIO 199W

• Out-of-department research (BIO 199X)

• Directed reading (BIO 198, 198X)

• No transfer courses can count toward the BIO 80-series

• HUMBIO Core cannot substitute BIO 80-series courses

rules.name: Biology Foundations Courses
rules.notes: • Additionally, students may count one additional Bio Foundations (80-level) Course toward the minor.

rules.name: GPA of 2.0 in the minor courses

gpa: Must earn a minimum GPA of 2.0.
grading: All courses must be taken for a letter grade (no other grading basis is allowed) and passed with a minimum of a C grade or better to receive credit for the minor.
policies: Department degree policies can be accessed in our Biology Handbook. Students interested in studying abroad can find more information in our Studying Away from Stanford.
transferPolicy:
Students are encouraged to have courses outside Stanford evaluated before taking the course at another institution. Course catalogs, syllabi, papers, exams, and/or lecture notes from the other institution are necessary for evaluation and accreditation. Transfer students are encouraged to contact the Student Services Office soon after arrival and with the Director of the Transfer Advising Program to review major requirements. Incoming transfer students can submit a Transfer Credit Evaluation form during the summer, but it will not be reviewed until the start of the Autumn quarter.
Students are encouraged to review the pre-approved course lists outlined by the Stanford University-wide Transfer Credit Database and Biology pre-approved transfer courses. The department authorizes transfer credit only for courses whose content parallels the Stanford courses and has comparable prerequisites (not merely a comparable course title). If transfer course(s) are not already approved at the university or department level, students should submit a Transfer Credit Evaluation Form. For full, detailed transfer credit instructions, please visit the Biology Transfer Credit website.
Students completing a Biology minor cannot use transfer credit or other external credit to substitute their BIO 80-series requirements
Credit for natural history, cultural biology, clinical, and similar courses is rarely appropriate and can be obtained only by meeting the same criteria outlined above. Verification of performance and the number of units is determined after completing the course. In some cases, students must provide exams, reading lists, term papers, and other materials for the evaluation.
reviewNotes: The audit checks six courses of at least 3 units each, all letter graded with a C or better: two BIO 80-series BioFoundations courses and four more from BIO courses numbered 100 and above (not the capstone, research or directed reading courses), the approved out-of-department list, or one more BIO 80-series course. BIOE 450 counts only once. At least three must be numbered 100 or above. You check the 2.0 GPA by hand.

totals.label: At least three courses at the 100 level or higher
